input.execution_flow: Command.main (core.py:1483) takes args from sys.argv[1:], expanding globs on Windows via _expand_args, or from the args you pass. It detects the program name and calls _main_shell_completion (line 1619). If the _<PROG>_COMPLETE env var is set, that function runs shell_complete and exits. Otherwise main opens `with self.make_context(prog_name, args, **extra) as ctx` and calls self.invoke(ctx). make_context calls parse_args. For each parameter, parse_args calls Parameter.handle_parse_result (core.py:2763), which does the following: consume_value picks a value and a ParameterSource; a deprecation warning is echoed to stderr if the value was set explicitly; process_value runs type conversion and callbacks; then the value is stored in ctx.params, with arbitration when several parameters share one name. Group.invoke dispatches to subcommands through resolve_command (core.py:2088). In standalone mode main then calls ctx.exit(). Exit, Abort, KeyboardInterrupt/EOFError, ClickException and EPIPE OSError are caught and turned into exit codes and messages. It has command/group factories, which turn a function into a Command or Group. It has the param-attaching decorators option and argument. It has preconfigured eager or flag options: confirmation_option, password_option, version_option, custom_version_option and help_option. Params are stashed on `f.__click_params__` until command() consumes them in reversed order, which gives top-to-bottom declaration order. Preconfigured options use kwargs.setdefault, so callers can override most defaults. version_option and custom_version_option force their own callback.

input.summary: src/click/parser.py is Click's private argv parser, adapted from optparse. Core.Command.make_parser (core.py:1227) builds an _OptionParser(ctx), and each Parameter's add_to_parser registers itself. Command.parse_args (core.py:1371-1372) then calls parser.parse_args. The parser does no type conversion or defaults. It returns raw values in a dict keyed by dest, the leftover args, and a list of parameter objects in command-line order. Unset values are the UNSET sentinel, and FLAG_NEEDS_VALUE marks an option whose value was omitted. The old public names (OptionParser, Argument, Option, split_opt, normalize_opt, ParsingState, split_arg_string) are served by a module `__getattr__` that emits DeprecationWarning.

interfaces.name: _OptionParser
interfaces.behavior: Internal parser class. __init__(ctx=None) stores ctx and defaults allow_interspersed_args=True and ignore_unknown_options=False. If ctx is given, both flags are copied from ctx. It starts with _opt_prefixes={'-','--'}, plus empty _short_opt, _long_opt and _args. The docstring carries a '.. deprecated:: 8.2' note.
edge_cases: ctx=None disables token normalization and resilient parsing
Flags are copied once at construction, so later changes to ctx are not seen

interfaces.name: _OptionParser.add_option
interfaces.behavior: Normalizes each opt string with _normalize_opt (which applies ctx.token_normalize_func). It builds an _Option, adds its prefixes to _opt_prefixes, and registers its short opts in _short_opt and its long opts in _long_opt. The dest is passed in explicitly and never inferred. action defaults to 'store' and nargs to 1. Valid actions are store, store_const, append, append_const and count.

An unknown action is not checked here; it fails later in _Option.process
Re-registering an opt string silently overwrites the earlier one

interfaces.name: _OptionParser.parse_args
interfaces.behavior: Builds a _ParsingState(args), runs _process_args_for_options and then _process_args_for_args. It returns (state.opts, state.largs, state.order). The input list is consumed (popped) in place.

input.summary: src/click/core.py holds Click's runtime model. Context carries per-invocation state: params, parameter sources, resources and cleanup. Command parses args and invokes the callback. Group, plus its CommandCollection subclass, dispatches to subcommands, including chain mode. Parameter, Option and Argument implement the value pipeline: parser value, then consume_value (env var, default_map, default, prompt), then type_cast_value, then process_value (required check, callback), then handle_parse_result. handle_parse_result also arbitrates when several params share one name. An internal UNSET sentinel is used throughout and is converted to None before the user sees it. ParameterSource is an IntEnum ordered from most to least explicit. Command.main wraps everything with exception-to-exit-code handling.

interfaces.name: ParameterSource
interfaces.behavior: IntEnum with members PROMPT, COMMANDLINE, ENVIRONMENT, DEFAULT_MAP, DEFAULT (enum.auto, so values 1..5). Lower means more explicit, so comparisons such as `source < ParameterSource.DEFAULT_MAP` mean 'explicitly provided'. handle_parse_result uses this ordering for deprecation warnings and for arbitration.
edge_cases: Ordering was changed in 8.3.3 (IntEnum, reordered)

interfaces.name: Context.__init__
interfaces.behavior: Builds a context for a command. Stores parent, command, info_name, params={}, args=[] and further settings. Key args: obj, auto_envvar_prefix, default_map, terminal_width, max_content_width, resilient_parsing, allow_extra_args, allow_interspersed_args, ignore_unknown_options, help_option_names, token_normalize_func, color, show_default. Several of these are None by default so they can be inherited from the parent or from the command (not re-read in full).
edge_cases: Settings default to None and are inherited from parent where applicable

interfaces.name: Context.scope
interfaces.behavior: Context manager that pushes the context onto the thread-local stack. With cleanup=False the context is not closed on exit. make_context uses it for parsing.
edge_cases: cleanup=False skips close()

interfaces.name: Context.with_resource
interfaces.behavior: Enters the given context manager, registers its exit to run on ctx.close(), and returns the entered value.

interfaces.name: Context.call_on_close
interfaces.behavior: Registers a callback to run when the context closes. Returns the callback, so it can be used as a decorator.

interfaces.name: Context.lookup_default
interfaces.behavior: Looks up name in default_map. If call=True and the value is callable, it is called. Returns None if the name is absent.
edge_cases: Callable defaults are invoked when call=True

interfaces.name: Context.find_object
interfaces.behavior: Walks up the parent chain and returns the first ctx.obj that is an instance of object_type, or None if there is none.
edge_cases: Returns None when absent

interfaces.name: Context.ensure_object
interfaces.behavior: Calls find_object. If it returns None, creates object_type(), stores it in ctx.obj and returns it.

interfaces.name: Context.fail
interfaces.behavior: Raises UsageError(message, ctx).

interfaces.name: Context.exit
interfaces.behavior: Raises Exit(code), default 0. Context.abort raises Abort.

interfaces.name: Context.invoke
interfaces.behavior: If the first argument is a Command, a sub-context is created. Every exposed param not in kwargs is filled from param.get_default (UNSET becomes None) and passed through type_cast_value. Then kwargs are recorded in ctx.params and the command's callback is called. If the first argument is a plain callable, it is called with the given args and kwargs. The call runs inside augment_usage_errors and the context.
edge_cases: A command without a callback raises TypeError
Defaults are type-cast but required is not enforced

interfaces.name: Context.forward
interfaces.behavior: Like invoke, but first copies all of the current ctx.params into kwargs for keys not already given. Only accepts Command objects.
edge_cases: A non-Command argument raises TypeError

interfaces.name: Context.get_parameter_source
interfaces.behavior: Returns the ParameterSource for a parameter name, or None if no source was recorded. Context.set_parameter_source sets it.
edge_cases: Returns None when unrecorded

interfaces.name: Command.make_context
interfaces.behavior: Copies context_settings into extra without overriding explicit keys. Builds self.context_class(self, info_name=..., parent=..., **extra). Then runs self.parse_args(ctx, args) inside ctx.scope(cleanup=False) and returns the context without invoking the callback.
edge_cases: Explicit **extra wins over context_settings

interfaces.name: Command.parse_args
interfaces.behavior: Raises NoArgsIsHelpError if there are no args, no_args_is_help is set and parsing is not resilient. Builds the parser and parses. For each param in iter_params_for_processing (eager params first, then in the order they were given on the command line) it calls handle_parse_result. Afterwards UNSET in ctx.params is converted to None. Leftover args cause ctx.fail('Got unexpected extra argument(s) (...)') unless allow_extra_args or resilient_parsing is set. Finally it sets ctx.args.
edge_cases: resilient_parsing suppresses errors
UNSET is converted to None only after all params are processed

interfaces.name: Command.invoke
interfaces.behavior: If the command is deprecated, echoes a red 'DeprecationWarning: The command ... is deprecated.' message to stderr. Then, if a callback exists, returns ctx.invoke(callback, **ctx.params). Returns None otherwise.
edge_cases: No callback means None is returned

interfaces.name: Command.main
interfaces.behavior: Uses sys.argv[1:] when args is None, with Windows glob expansion when windows_expand_args is true. Otherwise uses list(args). Detects prog_name, handles shell completion via the _PROG_COMPLETE env var and exits early. Runs make_context and invoke inside the context. With standalone_mode=True it calls ctx.exit() and ends with sys.exit. Exit sets the exit code. Abort prints 'Aborted!' and exits 1. EOFError/KeyboardInterrupt also lead to 'Aborted!'. ClickException is shown via e.show with e.exit_code. OSError with errno EPIPE is silenced, anything else is re-raised. With standalone_mode=False it returns rv, or e.exit_code for Exit, and re-raises Abort and ClickException. EOFError/KeyboardInterrupt are re-raised as Abort. Command.__call__ is an alias.
edge_cases: Exit in non-standalone mode returns the exit code, which is ambiguous with a return value
Chained commands can return [None, ...]

interfaces.name: Group.add_command
interfaces.behavior: Registers cmd under name or cmd.name. Runs _check_nested_chain(register=True) and stores it in self.commands.
edge_cases: No name raises TypeError

interfaces.name: Group.command
interfaces.behavior: Decorator that creates a command via decorators.command and registers it with add_command. Works with or without parentheses. Uses command_class when cls is not passed.
edge_cases: A bare callable together with kwargs triggers an AssertionError

interfaces.name: Group.result_callback
interfaces.behavior: Decorator that registers a result callback. It is called with (result, **ctx.params) after the subcommand runs. In chain mode the result is a list. replace=True allows replacing an existing callback.
edge_cases: Not read in full; replace semantics inferred from the signature

interfaces.name: Group.invoke
interfaces.behavior: Without a subcommand: if invoke_without_command is set, runs the group callback and passes its return value to the result callback (an empty list in chain mode). Otherwise fails with 'Missing command.'. In non-chain mode it resolves the command, sets ctx.invoked_subcommand, runs the group callback, builds the sub-context and invokes it, then runs the result callback. In chain mode it sets invoked_subcommand to '*' (or None), runs the group callback, creates all sub-contexts (allow_extra_args=True, allow_interspersed_args=False) and then invokes them in order. The result callback receives the list of results.
edge_cases: Group callback runs before the subcommand context is made
Chain contexts are all built before any runs

interfaces.name: Group.resolve_command
interfaces.behavior: Calls get_command(ctx, name of args[0]). If not found and token_normalize_func is set, retries with the normalized name. If still not found and parsing is not resilient: when the token looks like an option it re-runs self.parse_args(ctx, args) so that --help and similar are handled by the group. Then it raises NoSuchCommand with command-name possibilities. Returns (name, cmd, args[1:]). Under resilient_parsing it returns (None, None, rest).
edge_cases: Resilient parsing yields (None, None, ...)

interfaces.name: CommandCollection.get_command
interfaces.behavior: Checks the group's own commands first, then each of the sources in order. In chain mode it validates nested chains. list_commands returns the sorted union of names. add_source appends a Group to sources.
edge_cases: Source params and callbacks are not used
Own commands take precedence over sources

interfaces.name: Parameter.consume_value
interfaces.behavior: Value precedence: parser opts (COMMANDLINE), then envvar via value_from_envvar (ENVIRONMENT), then ctx.default_map via lookup_default (DEFAULT_MAP, including explicit None keys). A str from the default map is split via type.split_envvar_value when nargs != 1. Then get_default (DEFAULT). Returns (value, source), where value may be UNSET.
edge_cases: An empty envvar string is treated as unset
A key explicitly present in default_map with a None value counts as set

interfaces.name: Parameter.type_cast_value
interfaces.behavior: None becomes () for multiple or nargs=-1, otherwise None passes through. nargs==1 or a composite type: calls self.type(value, param, ctx). nargs=-1: converts each item into a tuple. nargs>1: requires exactly nargs items and returns a tuple. multiple: wraps the above in a tuple over the items.
edge_cases: A non-iterable raises 'Value must be an iterable.'
A wrong item count raises 'Takes N values but M were given.'

interfaces.name: Parameter.process_value
interfaces.behavior: UNSET becomes () for multiple or nargs=-1, otherwise it skips the cast. Otherwise calls type_cast_value. Then, if required and value_is_missing, raises MissingParameter. Then, if a callback is set, calls callback(ctx, param, value). UNSET is shown to the callback as None, and other UNSET params in ctx.params are temporarily masked as None.
edge_cases: The callback return value replaces the value
Option.process_value gives an unset non-required bool flag the value False, without type-casting (callback still called)

interfaces.name: Parameter.handle_parse_result
interfaces.behavior: Inside augment_usage_errors it calls consume_value, records the source, emits a deprecation warning to stderr if deprecated and explicitly set (source < DEFAULT_MAP), and calls process_value. In resilient_parsing mode, exceptions from process_value are swallowed and the value is reset to UNSET. When several params share a name, arbitration decides the winner: the more explicit source wins; on a tie the later one wins unless it would downgrade an explicit default. The winner writes ctx.params[name] if expose_value is true. Returns (value, args).
edge_cases: expose_value=False params are not stored in ctx.params
Losers restore the previous source

input.summary: termui.py is the public front-end for interactive terminal helpers. prompt/confirm loop over a module-level input function (visible_prompt_func = input, or hidden_prompt_func = getpass). style/unstyle/secho build and strip ANSI codes. progressbar, edit, launch, getchar, raw_terminal and get_pager_file lazily import their implementations from _termui_impl. echo_via_pager, clear and pause are implemented here, on top of get_pager_file, echo, getchar and isatty.

interfaces.name: prompt
interfaces.behavior: Prompts until valid input (termui.py:168-286). value_proc defaults to convert_type(type, default). Prompt text comes from _build_prompt: it appends Choice choices if show_choices, and ' [default]' if show_default is true and default is not None. A str show_default is shown instead of the default. Empty input returns the default if default is not None, otherwise it re-prompts. The default goes through value_proc like typed input. Uses hidden_prompt_func if hide_input, else visible_prompt_func, via _readline_prompt. confirmation_prompt=True uses 'Repeat for confirmation'; a str customizes it. A mismatch echoes 'Error: The two entered values do not match.' and restarts. A UsageError from value_proc is echoed as 'Error: {message}', and the message is masked with '***' if hide_input. KeyboardInterrupt and EOFError become Abort, with an extra newline echoed if hide_input.
edge_cases: default=None with empty input loops forever until input or abort
empty first value and empty confirmation value are treated as matching
a non-str default is cast to str only for typing; it still goes through value_proc
err=True redirects stdout to stderr during input()

interfaces.name: confirm
interfaces.behavior: Yes/no prompt (289-345). Accepts y/yes/n/no, case-insensitive and stripped. Empty input returns default unless default is None. Anything else echoes 'Error: invalid input' and repeats. The suffix shows y/n, Y/n or y/N via _build_prompt. abort=True raises Abort on a negative answer. KeyboardInterrupt and EOFError become Abort.
edge_cases: default=None requires an explicit answer
show_default=False hides the [Y/n] hint

interfaces.name: get_pager_file
interfaces.behavior: Returns a context manager yielding a writable text file for pager output (348-364). Resolves color via resolve_color_default, then delegates to _termui_impl.get_pager_file(color=...). Added in 8.4.0.
edge_cases: color=None means autodetect

interfaces.name: echo_via_pager
interfaces.behavior: Pages text (367-399). Accepts a str, an iterable, or a generator function; a generator function is called. Non-str elements are converted with str(). Writes each element to get_pager_file and flushes after every write, then writes a trailing newline (chained '\n').
edge_cases: a plain str becomes a one-element list
a generator object (not a function) is handled as a general iterable

interfaces.name: progressbar
interfaces.behavior: Builds a _termui_impl.ProgressBar (443-599) after resolving color. Defaults: show_eta=True, fill_char '#', empty_char '-', bar_template '%(label)s  [%(bar)s]  %(info)s', info_sep two spaces, width 36 (0 means full terminal width), update_min_steps=1. show_percent defaults to True only if a length is known

input.summary: src/click/formatting.py holds click's help-text layout code. It has a module-level FORCED_WIDTH override, the helpers measure_table, iter_rows, wrap_text and join_options, and the in-memory HelpFormatter class. HelpFormatter accumulates strings in a buffer and tracks the current indent. It provides write_usage, write_heading, write_text, write_dl, the section and indentation context managers, and getvalue. Width is measured with term_len, which ignores ANSI escapes. wrap_text delegates to click._textwrap.TextWrapper, which I did not read. Command.format_help and Group.format_help in core.py create the formatter through Context.make_formatter, which uses Context.formatter_class (core.py:315, 638-649).

interfaces.name: wrap_text
interfaces.behavior:
wrap_text(text, width=78, initial_indent='', subsequent_indent='', preserve_paragraphs=False) -> str. It calls text.expandtabs() first, then builds a click._textwrap.TextWrapper with replace_whitespace=False. Without preserve_paragraphs it returns wrapper.fill(text). With preserve_paragraphs it splits text.splitlines() into paragraphs at empty lines. The first line's leading indent (measured with term_len) is recorded per paragraph and re-applied through wrapper.extra_indent. Lines within a paragraph are joined with spaces. If a paragraph's first line is only ' ' (checked with strip()), the marker line is dropped and the remaining lines are kept verbatim through wrapper.indent_only, joined with '
'. Paragraphs are joined with '

'. Since 8.4.0, width ignores ANSI escapes.
edge_cases: Empty text returns '' without the initial_indent, which is why write_usage special-cases empty args.
A single leading '\b' paragraph keeps its line breaks and indentation.
Tabs are expanded to 8-column stops.
Styled long words are broken between visible characters (test_wrap_text_visible_width).

interfaces.name: measure_table
interfaces.behavior: Takes an iterable of row tuples and returns a tuple of the maximum term_len for each column index, ordered by column index.
edge_cases: An empty rows iterable returns ().
Rows of differing length are measured per index.

interfaces.name: iter_rows
interfaces.behavior: Generator that pads each row tuple with empty strings up to col_count. It does `row + ('',) * (col_count - len(row))`.
edge_cases: A row longer than col_count is yielded unchanged.
rows must contain tuples, because a list row would fail on tuple concatenation.

interfaces.name: join_options
interfaces.behavior: Takes option strings and returns (', '.join(sorted opts), any_prefix_is_slash). The prefix of each option comes from parser._split_opt(opt)[0]. Options are stably sorted by prefix length, so '-v' comes before '--verbose'. The flag is True if any prefix is exactly '/'.
edge_cases: An empty iterable returns ('', False).
Options with equal prefix length keep their input order.

interfaces.name: HelpFormatter
interfaces.behavior: HelpFormatter(indent_increment=2, width=None, max_width=None). max_width defaults to 80. If width is None it uses FORCED_WIDTH when set. Otherwise it uses max(min(shutil.get_terminal_size().columns, max_width) - 2, 50). Attributes are indent_increment, width, current_indent (starts at 0) and buffer (a list of str). Output is always in memory.
edge_cases: The computed width has a floor of 50.
An explicit width is used as given, with no clamp.

interfaces.name: HelpFormatter.write
interfaces.behavior: Appends the string to self.buffer with no processing. All other write_* methods go through it, so overriding it intercepts everything.

interfaces.name: HelpFormatter.indent
interfaces.behavior: Adds indent_increment to current_indent.
edge_cases: There is no lower bound check.

interfaces.name: HelpFormatter.dedent
interfaces.behavior: Subtracts indent_increment from current_indent.
edge_cases: It can go negative if unbalanced.

interfaces.name: HelpFormatter.write_usage
interfaces.behavior:
write_usage(prog, args='', prefix=None). The default prefix is _('Usage:') + ' '. It builds usage_prefix = f'{prefix:>{current_indent}}{prog} '. With empty args it writes usage_prefix.rstrip(' ') and '
' and returns. Otherwise, if width - current_indent >= term_len(usage_prefix) + 20, it writes wrap_text(args) with initial_indent=usage_prefix and a subsequent indent of spaces matching the prefix width. If not, it writes the prefix, then '
', then args wrapped with an indent of max(current_indent, term_len(prefix)) + 4. Both non-empty branches end with '
'.
edge_cases: Empty args gives 'Usage: prog\n' with no trailing space.
A styled prefix is measured with term_len.
The prefix is right-aligned to current_indent, so a prefix longer than the indent is not padded.

interfaces.name: HelpFormatter.write_heading
interfaces.behavior: Writes f"{'':>{current_indent}}{heading}:\n". A colon is always appended.
edge_cases: A heading that already ends in ':' gets a double colon.

interfaces.name: HelpFormatter.write_paragraph
interfaces.behavior: Writes '\n' only if the buffer is non-empty. This avoids a leading blank line.
edge_cases: It does nothing on a fresh formatter.

interfaces.name: HelpFormatter.write_text
interfaces.behavior: Wraps text with wrap_text(text, self.width, initial_indent and subsequent_indent set to ' ' * current_indent, preserve_paragraphs=True), then writes '\n'. The result honors the '\b' no-rewrap marker.

interfaces.name: HelpFormatter.write_dl
interfaces.behavior: write_dl(rows, col_max=30, col_spacing=2). The rows are materialised into a list. The first column width is min(widest term, col_max) + col_spacing. Each term is written at current_indent. If the term is empty-valued (second is empty) only a newline follows. If term_len(first) fits within first_col - col_spacing, it is padded to the column. Otherwise the description goes on the next line, indented first_col + current_indent. The description is wrapped with wrap_text(second, max(width - first_col - 2, 10), preserve_paragraphs=True). The first wrapped line follows the term, and the continuation lines are indented by first_col + current_indent.
edge_cases: Rows with a length other than 2 (including an empty rows list) raise TypeError.
Short rows are padded via iter_rows.
A second value that wraps to no lines writes '\n'.
The text width has a floor of 10.

interfaces.name: HelpFormatter.section

edge_cases: Dedent is guaranteed even if the body raises.

interfaces.name: HelpFormatter.indentation
interfaces.behavior: Context manager that calls indent(), yields, then calls dedent() in a finally block.

interfaces.name: HelpFormatter.getvalue
interfaces.behavior: Returns ''.join(self.buffer).
edge_cases: Returns '' if nothing has been written.

input.summary: src/click/exceptions.py defines Click's exception hierarchy. ClickException (exit_code 1) and UsageError (exit_code 2) can be shown to the user via show(). Subclasses cover bad or missing parameters, unknown options and commands, and bad option or argument usage. FileError is a ClickException. Abort and Exit are RuntimeErrors used only for control flow. NoArgsIsHelpError is also defined here and is not in the role description. Only FileError has a dedicated test file. I did not read core.py, docs, or the other tests that exercise these classes.

interfaces.name: ClickException
interfaces.behavior: Base class for exceptions Click catches and prints. __init__(message) calls Exception.__init__, caches show_color = resolve_color_default() because the context is gone by print time, and stores message. exit_code is a ClassVar equal to 1. format_message() returns message. __str__ returns message. show(file=None) writes 'Error: {message}' to get_text_stderr() (when file is None) via echo, using the cached show_color.
edge_cases: file=None defaults to stderr
show_color may be None

interfaces.name: ClickException.format_message
interfaces.behavior: Returns self.message. Subclasses override it to build the user-facing text, and show() always goes through it.

interfaces.name: ClickException.show
interfaces.behavior: Echoes the translated 'Error: {message}' line to the given file, or to stderr by default. Colour comes from the show_color cached at construction.
edge_cases: file=None means stderr

interfaces.name: UsageError
interfaces.behavior: exit_code 2. __init__(message, ctx=None) stores ctx and cmd (ctx.command, or None when there is no ctx). show() prints the usage text from ctx.get_usage(), then, if the command has a help option, a hint such as "Try 'cmd --help' for help.". The hint uses the longest help option name. After that it prints 'Error: ...'. The colour is ctx.color. Without a ctx it prints only the Error line, with color=None.
edge_cases: ctx=None prints only the Error line
no help option means no hint
hint picks max(help_names, key=len)

interfaces.name: UsageError.show
interfaces.behavior: Prints usage and the help hint when ctx is set, then the 'Error:' line, all to file (stderr by default).
edge_cases: ctx may be None

interfaces.name: BadParameter
interfaces.behavior: Subclass of UsageError. __init__(message, ctx=None, param=None, param_hint=None). format_message() chooses a hint in this order: param_hint, then param.get_error_hint(ctx), otherwise none. With a hint it returns 'Invalid value for {hint}: {message}'. With no hint it returns 'Invalid value: {message}'. A list or tuple hint is joined as "'a' / 'b'" through _join_param_hints, which applies repr to each item. Click fills in ctx and param itself when the exception is raised from a callback or type.
edge_cases: a str param_hint is used as-is
a sequence param_hint is repr-joined with ' / '

interfaces.name: BadParameter.format_message
interfaces.behavior: Builds the 'Invalid value for X: msg' text as described for BadParameter.
edge_cases: no hint and no param gives 'Invalid value: msg'

interfaces.name: MissingParameter
interfaces.behavior: Subclass of BadParameter. __init__(message=None, ctx=None, param=None, param_hint=None, param_type=None) passes message or '' to the parent. format_message() returns '{Missing X}{ hint}.{ msg}'. param_type defaults to param.param_type_name. 'argument', 'option' and 'parameter' map to the translated 'Missing argument', 'Missing option' and 'Missing parameter'. Any other value gives 'Missing {param_type}'. If param is set, param.type.get_missing_message(param, ctx) is appended to the message after '. ', or used on its own when the message is empty. __str__ returns the message, or 'Missing parameter: {param.name}' when the message is empty.
edge_cases: empty message is allowed
param_type=None and param=None gives 'Missing None'
with no hint there is no hint segment, so the text ends in '.'

interfaces.name: NoSuchOption
interfaces.behavior: Subclass of UsageError. __init__(option_name, message=None, possibilities=None, ctx=None). The default message is "No such option 'name'." The possibilities argument is filtered through difflib.get_close_matches(option_name, possibilities) (default n=3, cutoff 0.6) and stored as a list. It is None if possibilities is empty or None. format_message() appends 'Did you mean X?' for one match, or '(Did you mean one of: ...?)' for several, with names sorted and repr-quoted.
edge_cases: falsy possibilities gives possibilities=None
no close match gives an empty list, and the suggestion is omitted because the list is falsy

interfaces.name: NoSuchCommand
interfaces.behavior: Same shape as NoSuchOption, with command_name. It is marked versionadded 8.4.0. The default message is "No such command 'name'." Suggestions come from difflib.get_close_matches.
edge_cases: same as NoSuchOption

interfaces.name: BadOptionUsage
interfaces.behavior: Subclass of UsageError. __init__(option_name, message, ctx=None). It stores option_name and does not change the message. Used when an option is supplied but misused, for example with the wrong number of values.

interfaces.name: BadArgumentUsage
interfaces.behavior: Subclass of UsageError with no added behavior. Used for wrong argument usage, such as the wrong number of values.

interfaces.name: NoArgsIsHelpError
interfaces.behavior: Subclass of UsageError. __init__(ctx) uses ctx.get_help() as the message. show() echoes only format_message() with err=True and color=ctx.color. It has no 'Error:' prefix and no usage line. Its show() takes a file argument but passes err=True along with it.
edge_cases: ctx is required

interfaces.name: FileError
interfaces.behavior: Subclass of ClickException. __init__(filename, hint=None). The hint defaults to the translated 'unknown error' and is stored as the message. ui_filename = format_filename(filename) and filename is the raw value. format_message() returns "Could not open file {ui_filename!r}: {message}".
edge_cases: a surrogate filename is rendered with the replacement character U+FFFD

interfaces.name: Abort
interfaces.behavior: Subclass of RuntimeError with no extra behavior. It signals an abort and is not a ClickException.

interfaces.name: Exit
interfaces.behavior: Subclass of RuntimeError with __slots__ ('exit_code',). __init__(code=0) sets exit_code and does not call super().__init__. It is not a ClickException and is not exported in __init__.py.
edge_cases: it never calls Exception.__init__, so args is empty

input.error_conventions: ClickException subclasses are shown as 'Error: <message>'. UsageError and its subclasses have exit_code 2 and print usage plus a help hint first. Plain ClickException and FileError have exit_code 1. BadParameter messages read 'Invalid value for X: ...'. Missing parameters read 'Missing option/argument/parameter X.'. Unknown names read \"No such option/command 'x'.\" plus an optional 'Did you mean ...?'. All user-facing strings go through gettext (_ and ngettext). Names are shown with repr (!r). Abort and Exit are RuntimeErrors for control flow and are not shown as messages.

input.summary: src/click/shell_completion.py implements Click's tab completion. shell_complete() parses the `<shell>_<instruction>` value of the env var. It looks up a ShellComplete subclass in the `_available_shells` registry and either prints the shell script (`source`) or prints completions (`complete`). Command._main_shell_completion (core.py:1619-1649) calls it and then calls sys.exit with its return value. ShellComplete.get_completions resolves a Context chain (`_resolve_context`), picks the object that should complete (`_resolve_incomplete`), and calls that object's `.shell_complete(ctx, incomplete)`. That returns a list of CompletionItem. Each shell subclass reads COMP_WORDS and COMP_CWORD from os.environ and formats items in its own wire format. Bash, Zsh, Fish and PowerShell are built in. Other shells can be added with add_completion_class.

interfaces.name: shell_complete
interfaces.behavior: Does `shell, _, instruction = instruction.partition('_')`, then looks up the class with get_completion_class(shell). It builds `comp_cls(cli, ctx_args, prog_name, complete_var)`. For 'source' it writes `comp.source().encode()` with echo(nl=False) and returns 0. For 'complete' it writes `comp.complete().encode()` with echo (newline appended) and returns 0. Output is written as bytes so Windows does not turn LF into CRLF.
edge_cases: Unknown shell returns 1
Unknown instruction returns 1
A value with no underscore gives shell=whole string and instruction='', so it returns 1 unless the shell name is unregistered, which also returns 1

interfaces.name: CompletionItem
interfaces.behavior: Generic class with __slots__ ('value','type','help','_info'). `type` defaults to 'plain'. Click uses 'dir' and 'file' for special shell handling. `help` defaults to None. Extra kwargs go into `_info`.
edge_cases: __getattr__ returns None for any unknown attribute instead of raising AttributeError (`_info.get(name)`)
Extra kwargs are not used by built-in shells

interfaces.name: CompletionItem.__init__
interfaces.behavior: Sets value, type, help and `_info=kwargs`.
edge_cases: Arbitrary kwargs accepted

interfaces.name: CompletionItem.__getattr__
interfaces.behavior: Returns `self._info.get(name)`. It is only called when normal attribute lookup fails.
edge_cases: Missing keys give None

interfaces.name: ShellComplete
interfaces.behavior: Base class. Takes cli, ctx_args, prog_name and complete_var. Subclasses set the class attributes `name` and `source_template`, and implement get_completion_args and format_completion. complete() runs get_completion_args, then get_completions, then format_completion per item, and joins with '\n'.
edge_cases: The base class has no `name` or `source_template` defaults, so using it directly for source() fails
The tests use the base class directly for get_completions

interfaces.name: ShellComplete.func_name
interfaces.behavior: Property. Replaces '-' with '_' in prog_name, strips non-word ASCII characters, and returns `_{safe}_completion`.
edge_cases: Dots and other punctuation are removed (not turned into underscores)

interfaces.name: ShellComplete.source_vars
interfaces.behavior: Returns a dict with complete_func, complete_var and prog_name for formatting the template.
edge_cases: Subclasses can override this to add template variables

interfaces.name: ShellComplete.source
interfaces.behavior: Returns `self.source_template % self.source_vars()`, a %-style format.
edge_cases: Literal % in a custom template must be escaped as %%

interfaces.name: ShellComplete.get_completion_args
interfaces.behavior: Abstract. Returns (args, incomplete).

interfaces.name: ShellComplete.get_completions
interfaces.behavior: Calls `_resolve_context(cli, ctx_args, prog_name, args)`, then `_resolve_incomplete(ctx, args, incomplete)`. Then returns `obj.shell_complete(ctx, incomplete)`.
edge_cases: incomplete may be ''
`args` can be mutated, because an `--opt=val` incomplete appends the option name to it

interfaces.name: ShellComplete.complete

edge_cases: No completions gives an empty string

interfaces.name: BashComplete
interfaces.behavior: name='bash'. get_completion_args splits COMP_WORDS with split_arg_string and reads int(COMP_CWORD). args = cwords[1:cword]; incomplete = cwords[cword], or '' on IndexError. format_completion returns `type,value` and ignores help. source() first runs _check_version.

A non-integer COMP_CWORD raises ValueError
Help text is dropped

Tests patch it out with monkeypatch

edge_cases: Colon escaping applies only to items that have help text
The script is deliberately frozen for backward compatibility

interfaces.name: FishComplete
interfaces.behavior: name='fish'. COMP_CWORD holds the partial word itself, not an index. args = cwords[1:]. If incomplete is non-empty it is passed through split_arg_string(...)[0], and the same word is popped from args if it is the last one. format_completion returns `type,value` and appends `\t<help>` when help is set. In help, newlines are escaped as `\n` and tabs become spaces (8.4.2).

A quoted partial word is unquoted by the split

name='powershell' (added in 8.5.0). Same args logic as Bash, using an index COMP_CWORD. format_completion returns `type

Raises AttributeError if name is None and cls has no `name`

interfaces.name: get_completion_class

interfaces.name: split_arg_string
interfaces.behavior: Uses shlex.shlex(posix=True) with whitespace_split=True and commenters=''. If shlex raises ValueError (unclosed quote or trailing backslash), it appends the partial token `lex.token` to the output.
edge_cases: 'example \'my file' gives ['example','my file']

input.variation_strategy: Five features hit different layers: cross-parameter validation (core.py Option/Command.parse_args), a type's matching semantics (Choice), interactive input retry policy (termui.prompt), help-layout output (HelpFormatter), and filesystem type validation (Path). Each has its own interacting rule set (explicit-source eligibility, exact-vs-prefix precedence, attempt counting across error kinds, numbering/indent/width, suffix versus existence/dash/bytes).

features.title: Option conflicts_with and requires declarations
features.problem: Click has no declarative way to say two options are mutually exclusive or that one option needs another. Users hand-write callbacks that cannot tell explicit values from defaults.
behavior: conflicts_with and requires are sequences of parameter NAMES (the python names, as in ctx.params). Stored as tuples on the Option.
A parameter counts as 'explicit' if ctx.get_parameter_source(name) is ParameterSource.COMMANDLINE, ENVIRONMENT or PROMPT. DEFAULT_MAP, DEFAULT and no source are not explicit.
Checks run in Command.parse_args after every parameter has been processed (before leftover-args check). Params are examined in the order of command.get_params(ctx).

For each explicit option A and each name B in A.conflicts_with: if B is explicit, ctx.fail("Option 'A' cannot be used together with option 'B'.") where A and B are the parameter names (A.name, B) wrapped in repr quoting via single quotes, e.g. "Option 'json' cannot be used together with option 'csv'." The first violation found raises.
For each explicit option A and each name B in A.requires: if B is not explicit, ctx.fail("Option 'A' requires option 'B'."). conflicts_with checks for an option are done before its requires checks.
Conflicts are symmetric: declaring conflicts_with on only one of the two options is enough to trigger the error.
Failure is a UsageError (exit code 2) raised through ctx.fail.
interaction_rules: Only explicit sources count: an option that conflicts but whose value came from default or default_map does not trigger an error, and a required-by option satisfied only by default still counts as missing.
When option A both conflicts with C and requires B and both are violated, the conflict error is reported first.
